filestream-options-buffering.title: Configure file streams with FileStreamOptions
filestream-options-buffering.short: Group mode, access, buffering, and async settings in one object
filestream-options-buffering.summary: FileStreamOptions names the mode, sharing, buffer size, and FileOptions used when constructing a FileStream.
filestream-options-buffering.why: It makes a configuration easier to read than a long constructor argument list and keeps the intended I/O strategy explicit.
filestream-options-buffering.tips: A larger buffer is not automatically faster. Choose SequentialScan, Asynchronous, and buffer sizes to match the real access pattern.

utf8jsonreader-token-loop.title: Read JSON token by token with Utf8JsonReader
utf8jsonreader-token-loop.short: Parse forward without building a complete JSON DOM
utf8jsonreader-token-loop.summary: Utf8JsonReader is a low-level forward-only reader for UTF-8 JSON that exposes each token type and value as parsing advances.
utf8jsonreader-token-loop.why: Large JSON documents or selective extraction can be processed without materializing the entire document as JsonNode or another DOM.
utf8jsonreader-token-loop.tips: It is a ref struct with lifetime restrictions. For segmented input, also manage JsonReaderState and any unconsumed bytes correctly.

cryptographicoperations-fixedtimeequals.title: Compare secret byte values with FixedTimeEquals
cryptographicoperations-fixedtimeequals.short: Avoid content-dependent early exit when comparing authentication values
cryptographicoperations-fixedtimeequals.summary: CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals compares equal-length byte sequences while reducing timing differences caused by where their contents differ.
cryptographicoperations-fixedtimeequals.why: A comparison that stops at the first mismatch can expose information through timing when the compared value is security-sensitive.
cryptographicoperations-fixedtimeequals.tips: The API does not hide length. Use it for cryptographic byte values such as authentication tags, not as a replacement for ordinary string comparison.

volatile-read-write.title: Publish simple shared state with Volatile.Read and Write
volatile-read-write.short: Apply memory-ordering semantics to simple shared reads and writes
volatile-read-write.summary: Volatile.Read and Volatile.Write perform shared-value access with visibility and ordering semantics intended for communication between threads.
volatile-read-write.why: Plain field access alone does not express synchronization with another thread. Volatile operations can make a simple publication flag explicit.
volatile-read-write.tips: They do not make a sequence of operations atomic. Use lock, Interlocked, or another synchronization mechanism for compound invariants.

readerwriterlockslim-read-write.title: Separate read and write locking with ReaderWriterLockSlim
readerwriterlockslim-read-write.short: Allow concurrent readers while keeping writers exclusive
readerwriterlockslim-read-write.summary: ReaderWriterLockSlim provides distinct read and write locks so multiple readers can proceed together while writes remain exclusive.
readerwriterlockslim-read-write.why: For shared state with many reads and relatively few writes, it can reduce contention compared with one exclusive lock.
readerwriterlockslim-read-write.tips: Pair every entry with the matching exit in finally. For simple state, an ordinary lock may be safer and faster, so measure before adding complexity.

arraybufferwriter-growth.title: Build a growing contiguous buffer with ArrayBufferWriter
arraybufferwriter-growth.short: Write through GetSpan and commit bytes with Advance
arraybufferwriter-growth.summary: ArrayBufferWriter<T> is a growable in-memory IBufferWriter<T> that lends writable space and tracks committed elements through Advance.
arraybufferwriter-growth.why: Binary output with an unknown final size can be assembled without implementing array-growth logic manually.
arraybufferwriter-growth.tips: Do not retain spans or memory across operations that may grow the writer. Advance only by the number of elements actually written.

pipewriter-flush-complete.title: Write and flush buffered data with PipeWriter
pipewriter-flush-complete.short: Obtain pipeline memory directly and publish it asynchronously
pipewriter-flush-complete.summary: PipeWriter provides writable memory through GetMemory or GetSpan, then publishes committed data through Advance and FlushAsync.
pipewriter-flush-complete.why: Streaming producers and consumers can cooperate with fewer buffer allocations and copies than ad-hoc intermediate arrays.
pipewriter-flush-complete.tips: Advance only the bytes written, handle FlushAsync cancellation and completion, and call CompleteAsync when you own the writer and are finished.

enum-getvalues-generic.title: Enumerate enum constants with Enum.GetValues<TEnum>
enum-getvalues-generic.short: Retrieve declared enum values without typeof or casts
enum-getvalues-generic.summary: Enum.GetValues<TEnum>() returns the values declared by an enum as a TEnum array.
enum-getvalues-generic.why: Menus, diagnostics, and validation can enumerate enum constants while preserving the enum type throughout the code.
enum-getvalues-generic.tips: For a Flags enum, the result contains declared constants rather than every possible bitwise combination.

comparer-create-custom-order.title: Create local ordering rules with Comparer<T>.Create
comparer-create-custom-order.short: Turn a Comparison<T> lambda into an IComparer<T>
comparer-create-custom-order.summary: Comparer<T>.Create wraps a comparison delegate as an IComparer<T> that can be passed to sorting and ordered collections.
comparer-create-custom-order.why: A small local ordering rule can stay near its use instead of requiring a dedicated comparer class.
comparer-create-custom-order.tips: The comparison must define a consistent antisymmetric and transitive ordering. IComparer controls ordering and is different from IEqualityComparer equality semantics.

sha256-hashdata-span.title: Hash into an existing span with SHA256.HashData
sha256-hashdata-span.short: Compute one-shot SHA-256 without allocating a result array
sha256-hashdata-span.summary: The span overload of SHA256.HashData hashes an input and writes the digest into caller-provided storage.
sha256-hashdata-span.why: For one-shot in-memory data, it avoids creating a SHA256 instance or a separate result byte array.
sha256-hashdata-span.tips: For very large streams, consider incremental hashing. Do not use plain SHA-256 directly as a password-storage scheme.
